title: Introduce territory-constrained KMS consent gate and audit enricher
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds territory-based KMS proxy that attaches consent evidence to KMS requests, RBACv2 expression optimizations for territory grants, and audit enrichment that records non-identifying territorial hints and consent proofs. Backwards-compatible; rolled out as opt-in by tenant flag.
description:
Motivation: A subset of customers require explicit per-territory consent proofs and KMS key scoping that map to regulatory territories rather than cloud regions. Current KMS routing and RBACv2 grants are region-centric and do not capture consent artifacts required for audits. This change adds a lightweight territory-constrained KMS proxy and an audit enricher that attaches signed, non-identifying consent evidence to audit records.

What I changed: Implemented three coordinated components: (1) gateway middleware (territory_kms_proxy) that intercepts KMS wrap/unwrap calls and augments requests with territory assertions and consent blobs when the tenant opt-in flag is set; the proxy selects CMK aliases derived from a territory mapping table and performs a consent proof handshake with the consent store before forwarding to KMS. (2) RBACv2 expression optimizer: a small compiler that translates high-level territory grant templates into low-cost runtime predicates compatible with the policy engine; includes a caching layer to avoid policy recompilation on hot paths. (3) Audit enricher: instrumentation that records territory-hints and a consent-proof fingerprint into the encrypted audit envelope without including PII. The enricher also emits a separate high-cardinality telemetry metric used by security teams to monitor consent throughput.

Migration & rollout: feature is guarded behind tenant flag "territory_kms_consent_enabled" controlled in Console and via the Private Installer values.yaml. Default is off. We roll out in stages: internal e2e -> canary tenants -> wide rollout. There is a compatibility shim: if consent store is unreachable, the proxy falls back to existing region-based CMK selection and emits an alert with a safe-fail tag.

Testing: Unit tests for proxy handshake, RBAC compiler, and enricher serializer included. Integration tests simulate a local KMS stub and consent store in CI. One integration test flaked on initial CI run due to a race in the proxy cache invalidation; I fixed the race by switching to a mutexed LRU and added a deterministic eviction test. CI history: first run showed one flaky integration failure; rerun passed all checks.

Security review: reviewed with SEC-439 board. Threat model appended to docs: limits on consent blob size, signer verification in the proxy, and retention policy for consent fingerprints in the audit store. The KMS proxy authenticates using operator-scoped short-lived creds and uses a parameterized CMK alias scheme to avoid key alias collisions across tenants.

Docs & console: added a docs page under docs/security/territory-kms-consent.md and a small Console toggle (console/ui/consent-settings.tsx) for tenant admins to opt in and view consent history. Also updated the Private Installer chart values to include the new feature flag.

Rollout notes for SRE: New metrics (audit.territory.consent*), a healthcheck endpoint on the proxy (/healthz) and a new SLO target for consent handshakes (99.9% within 250ms). Updated alert: TerritoryConsentProxyUnhealthy with runbooks.

Commits (high level): Initial proxy and middleware + tests; RBAC expression compiler + unit tests; Audit enricher and integration tests; Fix race in proxy cache; Docs and changelog.

Why this is different: Rather than adding more region pins, this PR introduces a territory-first guardrail and includes audit-friendly consent proofs designed to satisfy regulatory requirements while minimizing PII surface in audit logs. The RBAC compiler keeps runtime policy checks cheap so we don't regress latency on hot paths.

Link to design doc: internal/eng/designs/territory-kms-consent (internal link).
